title: How to organise the bookshelves and display | Living Room
description:
Hold the books you will genuinely open again, and a small number of objects you actually want to look at.

This is the Bookshelves and Display in the Living Room. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Each shelf has a hand's width of empty space at one end, books standing upright between bookends with nothing stacked flat on top of them, frames and objects gathered in two or three groups instead of spaced evenly along every shelf, and a strap running from the top of the unit into the wall.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take one shelf down at a time so every book passes through your hands.
Straighten: Group by how you actually hunt for a book, which for most people is subject first and author second, never col
Shine: Dust the top edges of the books themselves, not just the shelf boards, and wipe the shelf fronts where hands g
Safety: Strap the unit into the wall studs, because a tall bookcase loaded high will come over when a child uses the s
Standardize: Bookends plus a small labelled marker at the front of each group makes a misfiled book visible from the doorwa
Sustain: When you finish a book, it goes back into its group that same evening instead of onto the coffee table.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every shelf keeps a hand's width of empty space, and the unit stays strapped to the wall.
